transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-01-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Evelyn Hart (CISO, Paladin), Marcus Reed (Platform Lead), Sofia Park (Compliance Manager)

Summary:
High-level compliance alignment and hosting options discussion. Paladin is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for inference workloads with emphasis on SOC 2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logging, KMS/HSM integration, and data retention rules for EU/US. Action items and POC next steps agreed.

Topics:
- Current infra and threat model
- SOC2 and ISO needs, timeline
- SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning
- RBAC and least-privilege for inference tokens
- Audit logs, retention, and log export
- Encryption: KMS, customer-managed keys, HSM requirements
- Data residency and retention policy mapping
- Deployment options: Hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private VPC

Transcript (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh Evelyn Marcus Sofia, we really appreciate you taking the time. We're Maya on the account and Diego's our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:12] Evelyn Hart: Hi all, Evelyn here, CISO at Paladin. We're looking at inference providers for our new compliance automation suite. Primary concerns are SOC 2 coverage, SAML SSO, and strict retention controls.
[00:22] Marcus Reed: Marcus Reed, platform lead. We'll own the POC and perf testing. Our stack is on GCP, k8s, some internal data plane in US and EU.
[00:28] Sofia Park: Sofia, compliance. We'll be mapping to ISO27001 eventually, and we have a set of regulatory retention rules for EU customer data.
[00:36] Diego Alvarez: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: run through redwood's controls, SSO/KMS options, audit logging export, then deployment alternatives and next steps.
[00:45] Maya Chen: One thing up front, Paladin, any hard constraints like must-have HSM or absolute no-hosted?
[00:52] Evelyn Hart: We prefer hosted for speed but if we can't get KMS separation or sufficient audit logs, we'd need Dedicated or Private. HSM is a strong preference for keys holding PHI-derived tokens.
[01:05] Diego Alvarez: Understood — Redwood Hosted supports BYOK via cloud KMS integration? small pause...sorry, that's our wording — we do support customer-managed keys in Hosted through KMS, and for HSM-backed keys we have Private deployment options that integrate with external HSMs.
[01:27] Marcus Reed: When you say Hosted KMS integration, is that cross-account IAM or do we need to rotate keys in your account?
[01:34] Diego Alvarez: Hosted uses per-customer CMK where feasible; it's an IAM cross-account encrypt/decrypt pattern with CMEK. There are some edge cases with model cache layers where we keep ephemeral keys for performance — that's documented in the security-runbook.
[01:48] Sofia Park: That "ephemeral keys for performance" phrase worries me; can we see the specifics in writing? We need to map key lifecycle to our encryption policy.
[01:56] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll share the key lifecycle doc and an appendix that explains cache key handling.
[02:02] Evelyn Hart: Good. Another thing: SOC 2 — do you have a Type II report?
[02:07] Maya Chen: Yes we do. I'll attach the latest SOC 2 Type II and our ISO readiness notes.
[02:12] Marcus Reed: What's in scope typically for inference — is model-serving included in SOC?
[02:18] Diego Alvarez: Yeah, our hosted control plane and serving runtime are in scope; for Dedicated we provide a separate control boundary and we can include dedicated pools in a SOC boundary via contractual commitments. For Private we hand off control plane but can arrange annual audits.
[02:36] Sofia Park: For Private, do you still provide audit logs or do we need to wire our own SIEM?
[02:41] Diego Alvarez: In Private we ship audit logs to your collector — we support syslog, Cloud Logging, and S3-style dumps. We can also enable log-forwarding to your SIEM with mutually agreed formats.
[02:55] Marcus Reed: Can you show an example log entry format?
[02:58] Diego Alvarez: I'll paste a sample in the follow-up, but it contains request id, model id, user token hash, timestamp, route, and result size. Note user tokens are hashed and we don't store raw upstream tokens.
[03:16] Evelyn Hart: Ok that's important. About RBAC — we have internal roles and need fine-grained controls for who can create inference keys and who can view logs.
[03:25] Maya Chen: Redwood supports RBAC with role templates (admin, dev, audit) and custom roles via SCIM. You can map your IdP groups to roles and require MFA for admin actions.
[03:36] Sofia Park: Do you have separation between billing view and security admins?
[03:40] Maya Chen: Yep, separate permissions for billing, metrics, and security — can be split into separate roles.
[03:46] Marcus Reed: On SAML/SSO — do you support SCIM provisioning? We don't want to manually create accounts.
[03:52] Diego Alvarez: Yes SCIM + SAML supported in Hosted and Dedicated; Private supports SAML and SCIM but provisioning may be integrated into your AD sync.
[04:03] Evelyn Hart: Data residency — can requests be pinned to EU region only? We have GDPR obligations for EU customers.
[04:11] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we can regionalize routing by policy. Hosted has EU regions and you can restrict a workspace to EU residency. Dedicated gives you more deterministic placement. Private is fully under your control.
[04:24] Marcus Reed: What's the typical audit log retention?
[04:27] Maya Chen: Default is 90 days in the console with export for long-term retention. You can set longer retention on export buckets; for enterprise we commonly configure 365+ days depending on regulation.
[04:37] Sofia Park: We need 7 years for certain records for one of our clients — is that feasible?
[04:42] Diego Alvarez: Yes via export to your storage (GCS/Azure Blob/S3) and lifecycle rules. We'll include a sample retention config.
[04:52] Evelyn Hart: How about access logging for model artifacts — who pulled the model, what version?
[04:58] Diego Alvarez: Model access is logged — model id, version, who invoked, and tokens hashed. Model artifacts themselves can be stored in your registry or Redwood's model catalog; for sensitive models we recommend private registries and Private deployment.
[05:12] Marcus Reed: On encryption in flight and at rest — what's not covered?
[05:16] Maya Chen: TLS 1.2+ in transit; at rest everything is encrypted. For Hosted, keys may be managed by Redwood or blue-cloud (cloud KMS) with CMKs; for customer-supplied CMK we support encryption at rest with CMEK for data at rest and envelope encryption for cache layers.
[05:33] Sofia Park: You mentioned cache layers and ephemeral keys earlier. Are those logged when used?
[05:38] Diego Alvarez: We log cache evictions and key rotations as events. The ephemeral keys are ephemeral by design and are rotated frequently — we will provide the rotation schedule.
[05:48] Evelyn Hart: Walk me through network isolation options for Dedicated — VPC peering or private link?
[05:54] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink-equivalent private endpoints. For Private we support full VPC deployed stack. We'll share a network diagram in the follow-up.
[06:06] Marcus Reed: For the POC — we want to benchmark latency and throughput. Do you have a test harness?
[06:12] Diego Alvarez: Yes Diego (me) will prepare a test plan that mirrors your typical payloads, batch sizes, and concurrency. We'll run it against a dedicated pool and a hosted endpoint to compare.
[06:22] Marcus Reed: Great. Any quotas or rate-limiting that will affect the POC?
[06:26] Maya Chen: We'll provision a dedicated capacity slice for the POC to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[06:31] Sofia Park: Regarding logs as evidence for audits — can you provide signed attestations or tamper-evident logs?
[06:38] Diego Alvarez: We support append-only signed log exports and can provide signed manifests for retained archives. For the highest assurance we recommend Private with dedicated log collectors.
[06:49] Evelyn Hart: Incident response — do you have an IR playbook and SLA to notify customers?
[06:55] Maya Chen: Yes we have incident response procedures. For enterprise customers we have 24/7 pager SLA and a structured notification timeline; we'll share the IR summary doc.
[07:06] Marcus Reed: What about encryption key compromise — can you rotate keys without downtime?
[07:11] Diego Alvarez: Key rotation is designed to be rolling; decryptors keep previous versions for a period so you can rotate without affecting serving, but there are performance considerations. We'll document a rotation window.
[07:25] Sofia Park: Can admin actions be logged to our SIEM and retained for the 7-year window?
[07:30] Diego Alvarez: Admin actions are part of audit logs and can be exported. For 7-year storage you would export and manage retention on your storage side.
[07:39] Evelyn Hart: Any certifications or third-party pen-test reports we can review?
[07:44] Maya Chen: Yes SOC2 Type II, and we've done third-party pen tests — we'll include redacted summaries and CVE remediation timelines.
[07:55] Marcus Reed: On the compliance checklist — we need a matrix mapping your controls to our control objectives.
[08:00] Sofia Park: Please include ISO mapping as well.
[08:03] Maya Chen: We'll provide a controls mapping matrix (SOC2 -> your control list) and an ISO gap report.
[08:09] Evelyn Hart: For SSO, can we enforce conditional access like IP restrictions or device compliance?
[08:15] Diego Alvarez: We support SAML with IdP-driven conditional access — enforcement happens at the IdP; Redwood honors the assertion. You can also bind session policies on our side.
[08:28] Marcus Reed: Are there any data exfil concerns with Hosted where raw request content might be cached in logs?
[08:34] Diego Alvarez: By default we hash tokens and redact sensitive fields in logs. We do not store raw customer payloads unless you opt into debugging exports, which are time-limited and audited.
[08:49] Sofia Park: So for debug sessions you store raw content — can we do that into our storage only?
[08:54] Diego Alvarez: Yes debug exports can be configured to write to your bucket with short TTL and access controls.
[09:02] Evelyn Hart: Timeline: we aim to finalize a vendor by end of Q1.
[09:07] Maya Chen: Good, that aligns with our standard enterprise onboarding timeline. We'll try to accelerate docs so you can evaluate before your procurement window.
[09:15] Marcus Reed: Any pricing difference for enabling CMK or longer log retention?
[09:20] Maya Chen: CMK has a small surcharge for Hosted due to key-management overhead; Dedicated/Private pricing differs — we'll send a comparative quote.
[09:29] Sofia Park: Contract terms — do you accept data processing agreements with EU SCCs?
[09:34] Maya Chen: Yes we have standard DPA with SCCs and can negotiate additional clauses.
[09:39] Diego Alvarez: Quick demo note — we can spin up a sandbox workspace for you to test SSO and KMS flows if you want to proceed to POC.
[09:48] Marcus Reed: Let's do that, sandbox plus POC for performance.
[09:51] Evelyn Hart: We'll need to loop in legal and procurement — Sofia will coordinate.
[09:56] Sofia Park: Yep will share contact details after the call.
[10:00] Diego Alvarez: I'll outline the test scenarios: 1) latency p95 under x ms 2) end-to-end KMS flows including rotation 3) audit log completeness 4) SAML provisioning lifecycle.
[10:12] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with SOC2, pen test summary, network diagram, and the controls matrix.
[10:18] Marcus Reed: For the POC, can you provide a rough capacity plan for 10k requests per minute?
[10:24] Diego Alvarez: We'll size that and include both batch and streaming paths — Diego will own the estimate.
[10:30] Evelyn Hart: Any outstanding red flags on your side?
[10:33] Maya Chen: Nothing we saw — just standard alignment.
[10:36] Marcus Reed: Ok let's recap next steps.
[10:39] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya send SOC2 + docs; Diego send perf test plan and sample logs; Marcus share infra diagram; Sofia share legal/procurement contact and retention matrix. Schedule sandbox POC kickoff for week of Jan 18.
[10:56] Evelyn Hart: Sounds good. Thank you.
[11:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc bundle.

(Notes: occasional transcription errors present — e.g., "K M S" instead of KMS, "redwood dedicate" instead of Dedicated in a few spots; speaker labels may drift in mid-segment.)
